newsitem.title: UK: Ireland must be weaned off EU aid - EU Commissioner.
newsitem.headline: Ireland must be weaned off EU aid - EU Commissioner.

text.p: Fast-growing Ireland needs to wean itself off regional aid from the European Union, European Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies said on Tuesday.
She told members of the House of Lords, Britain's upper chamber of parliament, that Ireland had been a great success story of the EU's regional development programme.
Between 1983 and 1995, Ireland's income per head increased from 63.6 percent of the EU average to 89.9 percent, according to figures from the Commission.
But Wulf-Mathies, the commissioner responsible for regional aid, said it was important for Ireland not to become dependent on the EU's structural and cohesion funds.
"Ireland has to face the task to prepare for...the future with a lot less European money than now," she told a House of Lords committee.

In his annual budget speech last week, Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn said it was uncertain how much funding Ireland would receive from the EU after the current four-year funding programme expires in 1999.

"The government will, in the forthcoming negotiations, argue that Ireland needs continuing substantial support," Quinn said, arguing that Ireland's recent economic progress was evidence that it used EU funds effectively.
But Quinn also said it was prudent to recognise that there could be no assurance that EU funding would continue indefinitely at present rates.
Wulf-Mathies repeated her suggestion that aid could be targeted better by channeling it to regions that account for 35 percent of the EU's population, down from 51 percent now.
